title: tallowbridge retinal outreach set selection
instruction:
You are Sasha Vasquez, the patient access supervisor at Tanneryside Clinic, preparing an outreach plan for Aneta Ainsworth and the Wintergate Board. We have 2,380 diabetic patients overdue for retinal screening, and the $11,500 outreach budget expires on 30 June. Aneta needs a defensible recommendation for the channel-and-staffing mix that will book the most confirmed screening appointments before the money disappears, rather than a general communications plan. The candidate outreach blocks, their costs, expected confirmed-booking yields, language reach, booking-clerk requirements, panel coverage, and operating restrictions are in `retinal_outreach_rules.xlsx`; use that workbook as the source of truth. Select the outreach blocks that should be funded and produce `retinal_outreach_allocation.xlsx` and `retinal_outreach_brief.pdf` in the top level of the working directory, using exactly those filenames. The spreadsheet should show the selected and unselected blocks, calculations for spend and confirmed bookings, coverage of every patient segment identified in the source, the booking-clerk and daily-capacity checks, the blackout period, and a comparison with the obvious all-overtime approach. The PDF should turn the same analysis into an approval-ready allocation recommendation for Aneta, including the chosen objective, assumptions, total spend, expected confirmed bookings, cost per confirmed booking, the comparison case, and any material operational trade-off. The two files must agree on every shared figure. Do not commit the full panel unless the selected blocks actually cover it, do not count a language segment twice merely because two blocks reach it, and do not invent conversion rates or patient groups that are absent from the source. Make a bounded recommendation using the supplied operating rules and have both files ready for review by 20 June.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/retinal_outreach_rules.xlsx` — Source-of-truth candidate outreach blocks, patient-segment coverage matrix, budget and booking rules, staffing limits, blackout dates, and the all-overtime comparison definition.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `retinal_outreach_allocation.xlsx` — An auditable outreach allocation workbook containing the candidate pool, selected set, formulas or transparent calculations, coverage checks, capacity and blackout checks, objective results, and comparison with the all-overtime case. (Save at the top level of the working directory with exactly this filename.; Use the codes, segment names, and policy definitions supplied in retinal_outreach_rules.xlsx.; Make selected versus unselected blocks and all shared totals easy to identify.; Calculations must be inspectable and must not rely on unsupported invented inputs.)
- `retinal_outreach_brief.pdf` — A concise approval-ready recommendation explaining the selected outreach mix, objective, budget use, expected bookings, efficiency, coverage, operating feasibility, and comparison with the all-overtime approach. (Save at the top level of the working directory with exactly this filename.; Use the same selected blocks and figures as the spreadsheet.; State the chosen interpretation of the objective and material assumptions.; Keep the presentation suitable for Aneta Ainsworth and the Wintergate Board.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
Retinal Outreach Allocation Recommendation
Tanneryside Clinic • For Aneta Ainsworth and the Wintergate Board

Decision requested. Approve the mixed-channel set below for Sasha Vasquez to place before the 30 June budget
expiry. Ready for review by 20 June 2026.

    Measure                           Recommended plan                               All-overtime alternative

    Selected blocks                   OT-06, VC-01, VC-03, VC-04, VC-05, SMS-01, SMS-02,
                                                                                     OT-01,
                                                                                         SMS-03,
                                                                                            OT-02,
                                                                                                 SMS-04
                                                                                                   OT-03, OT-04, OT-05, OT-06, OT-08

    Spend                             $11,400                                        $8,050

    Expected confirmed bookings       1146                                           605

    Cost per confirmed booking        $9.95                                          $13.31



Recommendation. Fund OT-06, VC-01, VC-03, VC-04, VC-05, SMS-01, SMS-02, SMS-03, SMS-04. The set
maximizes expected confirmed screening appointments (1146) while spending $11,400 of $11,500 ($100 remaining).
Cost per confirmed booking is $9.95. The all-overtime benchmark yields 605 bookings, so the recommendation adds
541 bookings (89.4%).

Operational feasibility. Every source segment is covered using explicit source flags; general-language blocks are
not credited for Spanish or Hmong. Spanish coverage comes from selected blocks marked Spanish-speaking, and
Hmong coverage from blocks marked Hmong-speaking, with language closing demand never exceeding the two
available clerks. Selected activity avoids the 23–25 June blackout and stays within each permitted date. Per-date
booking-clerk demand is at or below the two-clerk ceiling.

Assumptions and trade-off. Confirmed bookings are source-provided expected yields, not contacts or guaranteed
outcomes; binary segment coverage does not mean all 2,380 overdue patients will be reached or booked. The mixed
set requires coordination across vendor, SMS, mail, and overtime channels, but improves expected bookings before
funds expire.

Approval owner: Aneta Ainsworth • Prepared by: Sasha Vasquez, Patient Access Supervisor • Organization:
Tanneryside Clinic

spec.professional_context: Enterprise outpatient access planning for a rural health cooperative, where a time-limited outreach budget must be converted into a documented, operationally feasible booking plan.
difficulty_sources: Selecting a feasible subset across budget, language coverage, staffing, timing, blackout, and capacity constraints
Comparing a mixed-channel optimum with the obvious all-overtime alternative
Maintaining figure and selected-code agreement across a spreadsheet and an approval PDF
Making a bounded objective interpretation explicit without inventing unsupported patient or conversion data

reference_file.purpose: Create one offline workbook containing the complete finite set-selection instance and all rules the solver needs. Include a candidate pool of approximately 18 to 24 outreach blocks spanning staff overtime calls, vendor calls, SMS blocks, and mailed letters. Each candidate should have a unique code, channel, permitted date or shift window, cost, expected confirmed-booking yield, required booking-clerk capacity, and binary coverage flags for approximately 8 to 10 patient segments, including Spanish-speaking and Hmong-speaking segments. Include a policy section defining the $11,500 budget, the two available language-capable closing clerks, the per-day or per-shift capacity ceilings, the blackout window within the horizon, the 30 June expiry, the 20 June review deadline, and the exact all-overtime comparison case.
required_vocabulary: Use the candidate codes, segment labels, and policy labels in the supplied workbook as the canonical vocabulary.
The solver must reproduce those codes and labels in the deliverables rather than inventing alternate identifiers.

instance_design.objective: Maximize total expected confirmed screening appointments subject to all hard constraints. A secondary cost-per-confirmed-booking view may be reported, but it must not replace the declared primary objective without an explicit deliberate interpretation.
instance_design.patient_panel: Represent the 2,380 overdue patients through source-defined segments and coverage criteria; coverage is a binary requirement over segments, not a claim that each patient is individually booked.
hard_constraints: Selected candidate cost sum is at most 11500.
Every source-defined patient segment is covered by at least one selected candidate.
Language-specific segments require candidates explicitly marked as reaching that language.
Selected candidates must fit their permitted date or shift windows.
No selected activity may occur during the blackout interval.
Aggregate booking-clerk demand must not exceed the source per-day or per-shift ceiling.
Language-specific closing demand must not exceed the two available closing clerks.
All selected candidate identifiers must be unique and drawn from the candidate pool.
instance_design.comparison_case: Define the obvious all-overtime alternative as selecting the overtime-call blocks to the maximum extent allowed by the source's budget, timing, capacity, and staffing rules, with no vendor, SMS, or mailed-letter blocks unless the source definition explicitly requires them. Store its spend, expected bookings, and efficiency using the same formulas as the recommended set.
contention: Make several high-yield blocks compete for the same scarce daily or shift capacity.
Make language-capable blocks compete for the two closing clerks.
Include an internal blackout that makes at least one otherwise attractive candidate unavailable or partially unusable.
Ensure the all-overtime alternative is feasible but materially inferior, while the optimal set combines channels.
Include near-miss candidates that are attractive on yield or price but fail one stated threshold, timing condition, language requirement, or capacity condition.
instance_design.tightness_target: Approximately 0.70 to 0.78: feasible choices should be meaningfully constrained, with several locally attractive combinations failing capacity, language staffing, blackout, or budget checks. A simple greedy sort by yield or cost must not reliably produce the optimum.
instance_design.solver_gold: Enumerate or solve the binary selection model offline, record at least one optimal feasible set, and emit a checker that accepts any set satisfying all hard constraints and attaining the optimum primary objective. The checker should recompute coverage, capacity, blackout, spend, and expected bookings from the source rather than depend on a fixed row order.
derived_relationships: Expected confirmed bookings are the sum of source yields for selected eligible blocks.
Cost per confirmed booking is total selected spend divided by expected confirmed bookings.
Segment coverage is the logical OR of selected candidate coverage flags, with no double-counting across overlapping candidates.
Benchmark improvement is calculated from source-aligned selected and all-overtime values.
Cross-deliverable checks compare normalized candidate codes and unrounded underlying totals where available.

quality_controls: Verify offline that at least one feasible selection exists and that the solver identifies the intended objective optimum.
Verify that every enforced rule appears in the request or the supplied workbook, never only in this plan.
Generate a reference solution workbook and PDF, recalculate all figures, and walk every rubric item against them.
Set reference_solution_passed_rubric to true only after checking both computational predicates and rendered usability.
